We generated a novel reporter mouse that uncovers endogenous expression of the transcription factor Brn3b during development and in the adult retina and brain.

the development of new mouse models that allow for noninvasive monitoring of specific neuronal populations.
the generation of novel tools for studying the function of Brn3 in vivo.
the development of new genetic tools for the study of Brn3 proteins and RGCs.

our Brn3b reporter mice are a novel and valuable tool for studying Brn3b function in vivo and for monitoring retinal ganglion cell health in vivo.
